    - `BaseMongooseRepository` (`adapters/base/adapters.base.db.mongoose.ts`) — superclass for event, feed, feed service, device repositories.
    - `SimpleIdFactory` (uniqid) — feed ids and static icon ids; `MongoDbObjectIdFactory` — new ObjectId hex.
    - `MongooseDeviceRepository` (`adapters/devices/adapters.devices.db.mongoose.ts`).
    
    ##### Inputs
    `environment.mongo`: `uri` (`MAGE_MONGO_URL` || `mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/magedb`), `connectTimeout`, `connectRetryDelay`, `options` (pool sizes `MAGE_MONGO_MIN/MAX_POOL_SIZE`, deprecated `MAGE_MONGO_POOL_SIZE`, replica set, x509 key/cert/CA from env or files).
    
    ##### Processing flow
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
      W[waitForDefaultMongooseConnection] --> W0{readyState connected or connecting?} -- yes --> OK[resolve immediately]
      W0 --> R[RetryConnection.attemptConnection: log auth mechanism] --> C[mongoose.connect]
      C -- ok --> OK2[resolve]
      C -- err --> E{now < start+totalRetryTime?} -- yes --> T[setTimeout retryInterval] --> R
      E -- no --> X[reject 'timed out after ... seconds']
      B[BaseMongooseRepository] --> B1[create: model.create stub]
      B --> B2[findAll: find().cursor() streamed]
      B --> B3[findById]
      B --> B4[findAllByIds: find _id $in; map id->entity, missing->null]
      B --> B5[update: requires id; findById else throw; set stub; save]
      B --> B6[removeById: findByIdAndDelete]
      P[pageQuery] --> P1[limit pageSize skip pageIndex*pageSize] --> P2{includeTotalCount ?? pageIndex==0} -- yes --> P3[countDocuments]
    ```
    
    ##### Data
    `devices` collection (model `Device`, versionKey off): `uid` String required unique lowercase, `description`, `registered` Boolean required default false, `userId` ObjectId ref User, `userAgent`, `appVersion`. `getDeviceById(id, {populateUser})` optionally populates `userId`; note it returns the raw mongoose document (`query.exec()`), not the mapped entity. The `docToEntity` mapping (used by base methods) adds `user` = hex id or flattened user JSON with `id` hex, `roleId` from populated `role`, `authenticationId` from populated `authentication`.
    
    ##### Outputs & side effects
    Open Mongo connection; repository reads/writes.
    
    ##### External calls
    MongoDB via Mongoose; `uniqid` package.
    
    ##### Migration notes
    - Timeout message divides the absolute deadline timestamp (ms since epoch) by 1000, not the duration — the reported seconds value is wrong.
    - Retry also resolves if connection is merely `connecting`.
    - `pageQuery` returns totalCount only on first page by default.
    - `findAllByIds` keys result by `doc.id` (string) even for numeric ids.
    - Default doc mapping is `toJSON()`, so each schema's toJSON transform defines API shape.
    - `asyncIterable` helper maps async iterables lazily with optional `close`.

    Commentary: retry logic and timeout message quirk
    Code:
        attemptConnection(): Promise<mongoose.Mongoose> {
          log.debug(`attempting new mongodb connection to`, this.uri)
          if (this.options.authMechanism) {
            log.info('connecting to mongodb using auth mechanism ' + this.options.authMechanism)
          } else {
            log.info('connecting to mongodb without authentication');
          }
      
          return this.mongoose.connect(this.uri, this.options).then(this.resolve, this.onConnectionError.bind(this));
        }
      
        onConnectionError(err: any): void {
          log.error(`error connecting to mongodb database at ${this.uri}; please make sure mongodb is running: ${!!err ? err : 'unknown error'}`);
          if (Date.now() < this.connectTimeout) {
            log.info(`will retry connection in ${this.retryInterval / 1000} seconds`);
            setTimeout(this.attemptConnection.bind(this), this.retryInterval);
          }
          else {
            this.reject(`timed out after ${this.connectTimeout / 1000} seconds waiting for mongodb connection`);
          }
        }
      }
      
      export const waitForDefaultMongooseConnection = (mongoose: Mongoose, uri: string, retryTotalTime: number, retryInterval: number, options: mongoose.ConnectOptions): Promise<void> => {
        log.debug(`wait for default mongoose connection:`, uri)
        if (mongoose.connection.readyState === mongoose.STATES.connected || mongoose.connection.readyState === mongoose.STATES.connecting) {
          log.debug(`already connected to`, uri)
          return Promise.resolve()
        }
        return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
          const retries = new RetryConnection(mongoose, uri, retryTotalTime, retryInterval, options, resolve, reject)
          retries.attemptConnection()
        })
      }

    Code:
        async create(attrs: Partial<E>): Promise<E> {
          const stub = this.documentStubForEntity(attrs)
          const created = await this.model.create(stub)
          return this.entityForDocument(created)
        }
      
        async findAll(): Promise<E[]> {
          const docs = this.model.find().cursor()
          const entities: E[] = []
          for await (const doc of docs) {
            entities.push(this.entityForDocument(doc))
          }
          return entities
        }
      
        async findById(id: any): Promise<E | null> {
          const doc = await this.model.findById(id)
          return doc ? this.entityForDocument(doc) : null as any
        }
      
        async findAllByIds<ID>(ids: ID[]): Promise<ID extends string ? { [id: string]: E | null } : ID extends number ? { [id: number]: E | null } : never> {
          if (!ids.length) {
            return {} as any
          }
          const notFound = ids.reduce((notFound, id) => {
            notFound[id] = null
            return notFound
          }, {} as any)
          const docs = await this.model.find({ _id: { $in: ids } })
          const found = {} as any
          for (const doc of docs) {
            found[doc.id] = this.entityForDocument(doc)
            delete notFound[doc.id]
          }
          return { ...notFound, ...found }
        }
      
        async update(attrs: Partial<E> & EntityReference): Promise<E | null> {
          if (attrs.id == null) {
            throw new Error('update requires an id')
          }
          const found = await this.model.findById(attrs.id)
          if (!found) {
            throw new Error(`document not found for id: ${attrs.id}`)
          }
          const stub = this.documentStubForEntity(attrs)
          found.set(stub)
          const saved = await found.save()
          return this.entityForDocument(saved)
        }
      
        async removeById(id: any): Promise<E | null> {
          const doc = await this.model.findByIdAndDelete(id)
          if (doc) {
            return this.entityForDocument(doc)
          }
          return null
        }
      }
      
      export const pageQuery = <RT, DT>(query: mongoose.Query<RT, DT>, paging: PagingParameters): Promise<{ totalCount: number | null, query: mongoose.Query<RT, DT> }> => {
        const BaseQuery = query.toConstructor()
        const pageQuery = new BaseQuery().limit(paging.pageSize).skip(paging.pageIndex * paging.pageSize) as mongoose.Query<RT, DT>
        const includeTotalCount = typeof paging.includeTotalCount === 'boolean' ? paging.includeTotalCount : paging.pageIndex === 0
        if (includeTotalCount) {
          const countQuery = new BaseQuery().countDocuments()
          return countQuery.then(totalCount => ({ totalCount, query: pageQuery }))
        }
        return Promise.resolve({ totalCount: null, query: pageQuery })
      }

      const DeviceSchema = new mongoose.Schema<any>({
        uid: { type: String, required: true, unique: true, lowercase: true },
        description: { type: String, required: false },
        registered: { type: Boolean, required: true, default: false },
        userId: { type: Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'User' },
        userAgent: { type: String, required: false },
        appVersion: { type: String, required: false }
      },{
        versionKey: false
      })
      
      export function DeviceModel(conn: mongoose.Connection, collection?: string): DeviceModel {
        return conn.model(DeviceModelName, DeviceSchema, collection || 'devices') as any
      }
      
      export class MongooseDeviceRepository extends BaseMongooseRepository<DeviceDocument, DeviceModel, Device> implements DevicesRepository {
        constructor(
          model: mongoose.Model<DeviceDocument>
        ) {
          super(model, {
            docToEntity: doc => {
              let user: User | string | undefined = doc.userId?._id.toHexString()
              if (doc.populated('userId') && doc.userId) {
                const userJson = (doc.userId as UserModelInstance).toJSON<UserJson>()
                user = {
                  ...userJson,
                  id: userJson.id.toHexString(),
                  roleId: userJson.role ? userJson.role.id : userJson.roleId,
                  authenticationId: userJson.authentication ? userJson.authentication.id : userJson.authenticationId
                }
              }
      
              return {
                ...doc.toJSON<Device>(),
                user
              }
            }
          })
        }
      
        getDeviceById(deviceId: DeviceId, options?: DeviceReadOptions): Promise<Device | null> {
          let query = this.model.findById<DeviceDocument>(deviceId);
          if (options?.populateUser) {
            query = query.populate('userId')
          }
      
          return query.exec()
        }

    - `mageAppErrorHandler` / `compatibilityMageAppErrorHandler` — router-level error handlers.
    - `httpRequestLogging(log.child({component:'http'}), env.httpRequestLogMethods)` (`adapters.logging.http.ts`) — registered globally in `express.ts` via `app.use`.
    - `access.authorize(permission)` (`access/index.ts`) — legacy route middleware (45 import sites in legacy routes).
    - `@types/express/index.d.ts` — type augmentation: `req.user: UserDocument & any`, `req.provisionedDeviceId: string`, `req.getRoot()`, `req.getPath()`.
    
    ##### Inputs
    Express request: `req.params.eventScope`, `req.user` (passport), `req.body.username` (for logging), method/path/originalUrl.

    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
      E[ensureEventScope] --> E1[parseInt params.eventScope]
      E1 -- not integer --> E404[404 json 'event not found: raw']
      E1 --> E2[eventRepo.findById -> MageEvent] -- null --> E404
      E2 --> E3[req.eventScope = mageEvent; next]
      H[mageAppErrorHandler] --> H0[console.error] --> H1{MageError?} -- no --> N[next err]
      H1 --> H2{code} -- PermissionDenied --> S403[403 'permission denied: perm']
      H2 -- EntityNotFound --> S404[404 message]
      H2 -- InvalidInput --> S400[400]
      H2 -- Infrastructure --> S500[500]
      H2 -- other --> N
      L[httpRequestLogging] --> L0{path under /api,/auth,/plugins?} -- no --> next
      L0 --> L1[on finish: user=username or anonymous; redact access_token]
      L1 --> L2{status 401/403?} -- yes --> warn
      L2 --> L3{method in configured set?} -- no --> skip
      L3 --> L4{POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE?} -- yes --> info
      L4 -- no --> debug
      A[access.authorize perm] --> A0{req.user?} -- no --> next2[next - NOT denied]
      A0 --> A1{user.roleId populated role?} -- no --> F403[403]
      A1 --> A2{role.permissions includes perm?} -- no --> F403
      A2 --> next3[next]
    ```
    
    ##### Data
    Event lookup reads `events` by numeric `_id`. Logging meta: `{user, userId, status, duration ms, attemptedUser?}` where `attemptedUser` = `req.body.username` when unauthenticated.
    
    ##### Outputs & side effects
    404/403/400/500 JSON responses; log lines `METHOD sanitizedUrl`.
    
    ##### External calls
    None (logger from entities.logging).
    
    ##### Migration notes
    - `parseInt` accepts prefixes: `/api/events/12abc/...` resolves event 12.
    - Error body shape differs: `mageAppErrorHandler` sends a bare JSON string, `compatibility...` sends `{message}`; legacy clients expect the latter. Only the event exports POST router uses the bare-string variant.
    - `authorize()` passes through when there is no `req.user` — it relies on authentication middleware having run earlier; `roleId` must be a populated Role document.
    - Only the first `access_token=` occurrence in the URL is redacted; 401/403 are always logged at warn even if method excluded.
    - Default logged methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.

      export function ensureEventScope(eventRepo: MageEventRepository): express.RequestHandler {
        return async (req: express.Request, res: express.Response, next: express.NextFunction): Promise<void> => {
          const eventIdFromPath = req.params[eventScopeKey]
          const eventId: MageEventId = parseInt(eventIdFromPath)
          const mageEvent = Number.isInteger(eventId)
            ? await eventRepo.findById(eventId)
            : null
          if (mageEvent) {
            req[eventScopeKey] = { mageEvent }
            next()
            return
          }
          res.status(404).json(`event not found: ${eventIdFromPath}`)
        }
      }
      
      declare module 'express' {
        interface Request {
          [eventScopeKey]?: {
            mageEvent: MageEvent
          }
        }
      }
      
      /**
       * Send HTTP responses with status codes that map to error codes of
       * {@link MageError} instances from the application layer.  For example, send
       * a `403` response for {@link ErrPermissionDenied}.
       */
      export const mageAppErrorHandler: express.ErrorRequestHandler = (err: any, req: express.Request, res: express.Response, next: express.NextFunction): any  => {
        console.error(new Date().toISOString(), '- error processing request', req.method, req.path, err)
        if (!(err instanceof MageError)) {
          return next(err)
        }
        switch (err.code) {
          case ErrPermissionDenied:
            return res.status(403).json(`permission denied: ${(err as PermissionDeniedError).data.permission}`)
          case ErrEntityNotFound:
            return res.status(404).json(err.message)
          case ErrInvalidInput:
            return res.status(400).json(err.message)
          case ErrInfrastructure:
            return res.status(500).json(err.message)
        }
        next(err)
      }
      
      /**
       * This is the same as {@link mageAppErrorHandler}, but instead of just a bare
       * JSON string as the request body, sends a JSON object as the response like
       * ```
       * { "message": "the error message" }
       * ```
       * This is what clients expect from the legacy routes, so new routes that
       * replace them need to send errors in this structure.
       */
      export const compatibilityMageAppErrorHandler: express.ErrorRequestHandler = (err: any, req: express.Request, res: express.Response, next: express.NextFunction): any  => {
        console.error(new Date().toISOString(), '- error processing request', req.method, req.path, err)
        if (!(err instanceof MageError)) {
          return next(err)
        }
        switch (err.code) {
          case ErrPermissionDenied:
            return res.status(403).json({ message: `permission denied: ${(err as PermissionDeniedError).data.permission}` })
          case ErrEntityNotFound:
            return res.status(404).json({ message: err.message })
          case ErrInvalidInput:
            return res.status(400).json({ message: err.message })
          case ErrInfrastructure:
            return res.status(500).json({ message: err.message })
        }
        next(err)
      }

      export function httpRequestLogging(log: Logger, loggedMethods: string[] = defaultLoggedMethods): express.RequestHandler {
        const methods = new Set(loggedMethods.map(m => m.trim().toUpperCase()).filter(m => m.length > 0))
        return (req, res, next) => {
          if (!loggedPathPrefixes.some(p => req.path === p || req.path.startsWith(p + '/'))) {
            return next()
          }
          const start = Date.now()
          res.on('finish', () => {
            const principal = req.user as { id?: string, username?: string } | undefined
            const user = principal?.username ?? 'anonymous'
            const message = `${req.method} ${sanitizeUrl(req.originalUrl)}`
            const meta: Record<string, unknown> = { user, userId: principal?.id, status: res.statusCode, duration: Date.now() - start }
            if (!principal) {
              const attempted = (req.body as { username?: unknown } | undefined)?.username
              if (typeof attempted === 'string' && attempted) {
                meta.attemptedUser = attempted
              }
            }
            if (res.statusCode === 401 || res.statusCode === 403) {
              log.warn(message, meta)
            }
            else if (!methods.has(req.method)) {
              return
            }
            else if (mutatingMethods.has(req.method)) {
              log.info(message, meta)
            }
            else {
              log.debug(message, meta)
            }
          })
          next()
        }
      }

        authorize(permission: AnyPermission): express.RequestHandler {
          return function(req, res, next): any {
            if (!req.user) {
              return next()
            }
            const role = req.user.roleId as Role
            if (!role) {
              return res.sendStatus(403)
            }
            const userPermissions = role.permissions
            const ok = userPermissions.indexOf(permission) !== -1
            if (!ok) {
              return res.sendStatus(403)
            }
            next()

    ```mermaid
      C[GET /:iconId/content] --> C1[GetStaticIconContent: no permission check] --> C2[repo.loadContent id]

      C2 -- sourceUrl --> C3[loadRemoteContent fetch/cached]

      C3 & C4 --> C5[res.type mediaType; cache-control private max-age=31536000; pipe 200]
      C2 -- Error --> X5[iconSourceUrlFetchError]
      G[GET /:iconId] --> G1[findByReference id] -- none --> G404[404 'icon not found: id']
      G1 --> G2[json + contentPath baseUrl/id/content]
      S[GET /?source_url] --> S0{valid URL?} -- no --> S400[400 invalid icon source url]
      S0 --> S1[findByReference sourceUrl] -- none --> S2[200 null]
      L[GET / list] --> L1[repo.find paging] --> L2[items + contentPath]
      P[POST /] --> P0[busboy init] -- throws --> P400[400 message]
      P0 --> P1[pipe req to busboy]
      P1 -- file 'icon' --> P2[CreateStaticIcon: STATIC_ICON_WRITE perm] --> P3[repo.createLocal: id=uniqid, registeredTimestamp=now; putContent; model.create]
      P1 -- other file/field/limits --> P4[400 \"request must contain only one file part named 'icon'\"]
      P3 --> P5[after busboy close: res.json icon]
    ```
    Upload response is deferred via the `afterUploadStream` event until busboy emits `close`; only the first queued finisher is registered (`listenerCount` check) so the first outcome wins.

    - Icon content files: `environment.iconBaseDirectory` = `MAGE_ICON_DIR` || `/var/lib/mage/icons`; path `<YYYY>/<MM>/<iconId>` using UTC year and zero-padded UTC month of `registeredTimestamp`; mkdir -p then `writeFile(stream)`. Read via `open(...).createReadStream()`; ENOENT -> ContentNotFound else StorageError.
    - Icon metadata in Mongo via `adapters.icons.db.mongoose.ts` (outside batch): `create({...icon, _id:id})`, `findById`.
    
    ##### Outputs & side effects
    Icon JSON + `contentPath`; list `{...page, items:[...+contentPath]}`; raw bytes with `Content-Type` = stored mediaType; file + DB record on upload; console logs.
    
    ##### External calls
    `busboy` multipart parser; remote icon fetch for sourceUrl icons (in icons repository, not traced).
    
    ##### Migration notes
    - Read permission `ensureGetStaticIconPermission` always returns null (any bearer user); write requires `STATIC_ICON_WRITE`.
    - In `createLocal`, content is written BEFORE the DB record; `putContent` returns (doesn't throw) StorageError which is ignored, so a DB record can exist without content.
    - Unknown source_url returns 200 `null`, unknown id returns 404 — asymmetric.
    - `etag` computed but not sent (commented out).
    - Uploaded mediaType is client-supplied and replayed as Content-Type.
    - `contentPath` is relative (`req.baseUrl`), not absolute.

    Commentary: busboy upload lifecycle
    Code:
          .post(
            (req, res, next) => {
              /*
              encapsulate the busboy init in a middleware so the request can
              fail-fast when busboy throws a validation error
              */
              try {
                req.iconUpload = busboy({
                  headers: req.headers,
                  limits: { files: 1, fields: 0 }
                })
              } catch (err) {
                console.error('error initializing icon upload\n', req.params, '\nheaders:\n', req.headers, '\n', err)
                return res.status(400).json({ message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) })
              }
              next()
            },
            async (req, res, next) => {
              const afterUploadStreamEvent = 'afterUploadStream'
              const sendInvalidRequestStructure = () => next(invalidInput("request must contain only one file part named 'icon'"))
              const afterUploadStream = (finishResponse: () => void) => {
                if (req.iconUpload?.listenerCount(afterUploadStreamEvent)) {
                  return
                }
                if (req.iconUpload?.writable) {
                  return void(req.iconUpload.on(afterUploadStreamEvent, finishResponse))
                }
                finishResponse()
              }
              req.pipe(req.iconUpload!
                .on('file', async (fieldName, stream, info: FileInfo) => {
                  if (fieldName !== 'icon') {
                    // per busboy docs, drain the file stream and move on
                    console.error(`unexpected file entry '${fieldName}' uploading icon`)
                    stream.resume()
                    return afterUploadStream(sendInvalidRequestStructure)
                  }
      
                  const iconInfo: LocalStaticIconStub = {
                    title: 'StaticIcon',
                    mediaType: info.mimeType,
                    fileName: info.filename
                  }
      
                  const appReq: CreateLocalStaticIconRequest = createAppRequest(req, { iconContent: stream, iconInfo: iconInfo })
                  const appRes = await appLayer.createIcon(appReq)
                  if (appRes.success) {
                    console.info(`successfully stored static icon ${appRes.success.id}`)
                    return void(afterUploadStream(() => {
                      res.json({...appRes.success})
                    }))
                  }
                  if (appRes.error) {
                    afterUploadStream(() => next(appRes.error))
                  } else {
                    afterUploadStream(sendInvalidRequestStructure)
                  }
                  /*
                  per busboy docs, drain the stream and ignore the contents; necessary
                  for the busboy stream to terminate properly
                  */
                  stream.resume()
                })
                .on('field', (fieldName, content, info) => {
                  console.error(`unexpected field ${fieldName} uploading icon`)
                  afterUploadStream(sendInvalidRequestStructure)
                })
                .on('filesLimit', () => {
                  console.error(`too many file parts in upload request for icon`)
                  afterUploadStream(sendInvalidRequestStructure)
                })
                .on('fieldsLimit', () => {
                  console.error(`too many field parts in upload request for icon`)
                  afterUploadStream(sendInvalidRequestStructure)
                })
                .on('close', () => {
                  req.iconUpload?.emit(afterUploadStreamEvent)
                  req.iconUpload?.removeAllListeners()
                })
              )
            }
          )

    Commentary: icon directory layout
    Code:
        async putContent(icon: StaticIcon, content: NodeJS.ReadableStream): Promise<void | StaticIconStoreError> {
          const relativePath = relativeWritePathForIcon(icon)
          const absolutePath = path.join(this.baseDirPath, relativePath)
          try {
            await mkdir(path.dirname(absolutePath), { recursive: true })
            await writeFile(absolutePath, content)
          } catch (err) {
            return new StaticIconStoreError(StaticIconStoreErrorCode.StorageError, `error writing icon content to ${absolutePath}`)
          }
        }
      
        async loadContent(icon: StaticIcon): Promise<NodeJS.ReadableStream | StaticIconStoreError> {
          const relativePath = relativeWritePathForIcon(icon)
          const contentPath = path.join(this.baseDirPath, relativePath)
      
          try {
            const fileHandle = await open(contentPath, 'r')
            return fileHandle.createReadStream()
          } catch (err) {
            const errno = err as NodeJS.ErrnoException
            const code = errno && errno.code === 'ENOENT' ? StaticIconStoreErrorCode.ContentNotFound : StaticIconStoreErrorCode.StorageError
            return new StaticIconStoreError(code, `error reading static icon ${icon.id}`)
          }
        }
      }
      
      function relativeWritePathForIcon(icon: StaticIcon): string {
        const registered = new Date(icon.registeredTimestamp)
        return path.join(
          String(registered.getUTCFullYear()),
          String(registered.getUTCMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0'),
          icon.id
        )
      }

    Two Express routers built in `adapters.exports.controllers.web.ts` and mounted in `app.ts` `initWebLayer`:
    - `ExportRoutes(app.exports, eventScopedRequestFactory)` at `/api/events/:eventScope/exports` with middleware `[bearerAuthentication, ensureEventScope(eventRepo), exportRoutes]`.
      - `POST /api/events/:eventId/exports` -> `appLayer.createExport` (`CreateExport` in `app.impl/exports/app.impl.exports.ts`).
    - `MyExportRoutes(app.exports, appRequestFactory)` at `/api/exports/mine` with `[bearerAuthentication, myExportRoutes]` (no event scope).
      - `GET /api/exports/mine` -> `appLayer.getExports` (`FetchExports`).
      - `GET /api/exports/mine/:exportId` -> `appLayer.getExportContent` (`GetExportContent`).
      - `DELETE /api/exports/mine/:exportId` -> `appLayer.deleteExport` (`DeleteExport`).
    
    Note: neither router installs `express.json()`; `req.body` on POST relies on the global body parser configured in `express.ts` (legacy layer).
    
    ##### Inputs
    **POST body** (parsed by `parseExportCreateParams`):
    ```
    {
      format: 'kml'|'geojson'|'geopackage'|'csv'   // required, EXPORT_FORMATS
      observations?: {
        startDate?: ISO-8601 string, endDate?: ISO-8601 string,
        includeAttachments?: boolean (default true),
        favorites?: any (truthy => only requester's favorites),
        important?: any (passed through as isFlaggedImportant),
        users?: string[], teams?: string[],      // ignored unless arrays
        hasAttachments?: any (falsy -> undefined),
        keyword?: string (only if non-empty string),
        condition?: any (parseConditionFilter from app.api.observations),
        projection?: [{ formId, fields: string[] }]  // ignored unless array
      },
      locations?: { startDate?, endDate?, users?: string[], teams?: string[] }
    }
    ```
    Dates are parsed with `utilities/dates.parseISO8601`; falsy date -> undefined; unparsable -> 400 `Export <observations|locations>.<startDate|endDate> must be a valid ISO-8601 date.`
    
    **Path params**: `:eventScope` (integer event id, see ensureEventScope), `:exportId` (Mongo ObjectId hex).
    **Auth context**: `req.user` (passport bearer) -> `context.requestingPrincipal()`; event-scoped context adds `mageEvent`.
    
    ##### Processing flow
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
      A[POST /api/events/:eventScope/exports] --> B[bearerAuthentication]
      B --> C[ensureEventScope: parseInt + eventRepo.findById]
      C -- not found/NaN --> C404[404 json 'event not found: id']
      C --> D[parseExportCreateParams]
      D -- missing format --> E400[InvalidInput -> mageAppErrorHandler 400]
      D -- format not in EXPORT_FORMATS --> E400
      D -- bad date --> E400
      D --> F[CreateExport: ensureCreateExportPermission\nuserHasEventPermission Read]
      F -- denied --> E403[403 'permission denied: CREATE EXPORT']
      F --> G[MongooseExportsRepository.createExport status=Running\nexpirationDate=now+exportTtl]
      G --> H[exportFactory format]
      H -- null --> E400b[invalidInput 'invalid export type' - record already created]
      H --> I[FileSystemExportContentStore.writeContent -> id-type.zip write stream]
      I --> J[updateExportForUser status=Running relativePath]
      J --> K[resolveUserIsAnyOf teams->users; build findSpecs]
      K --> L[archiver zip piped to file; exporter.export async, NOT awaited]
      L --> R[respond jsonForExport + url]
      L -.success.-> M[archive.finalize; wait close; contentStats size; update status=Completed size summary; log]
      L -.error.-> N[deleteContent; update status=Failed; archive.abort]
      subgraph mine[/api/exports/mine]
       P1[GET /] --> P2[getExportsForUser sorted _id desc, populated] --> P3[json array with url]
       Q1[GET /:exportId] --> Q2[getExportForUser id+userId] -- null --> Q404[404]
       Q2 --> Q3[readContent open file] -- ENOENT/err --> Q500[500 infrastructure]
       Q3 --> Q4[200 application/zip, content-length=size, pipe]
       S1[DELETE /:exportId] --> S2[deleteExportForUser] -- null --> S404[404]
       S2 --> S3[deleteContent unlink; errors ignored] --> S4[204]
      end
    ```
    Steps for create (in order):
    1. Validate body (above). Filter object built only with provided `observations`/`locations` keys.
    2. Permission: `RoleBasedExportsPermissionService.ensureCreateExportPermission` — allowed iff `eventPermissions.userHasEventPermission(mageEvent, user.id, Read)`; otherwise `permissionDenied('CREATE EXPORT', user.id)`.
    3. `exportsRepository.createExport({ userId, eventId: mageEvent.id, ...req })` — note `...req` spreads `format`, `filter`, `context` into the attrs; repository picks `format`, `filter`, `relativePath`, `filename` (the latter two are undefined at this point).
    4. `exportFactory(format)`; if null returns invalidInput — but the export document already exists with status Running and is never cleaned (until TTL sweep or restart sweep marks it Failed).
    5. Content stream created at `<exportDirectory>/<exportId>-<format>.zip`; document patched with `relativePath`.
    6. Observation findSpec: `stateIsAnyOf:['active']`, `timestampAfter/Before`, `isFavoriteOfUser: favorites ? user.id : undefined`, `isFlaggedImportant: important`, `userIsAnyOf` (union of users and team members via `resolveUserIsAnyOf`), `hasAttachments`, `fieldFilter`, `includeAttachments`; plus `projection`.
       Location findSpec: `eventId`, `timestampAfter/Before`, `userIsAnyOf`.
    7. Zip archive generated asynchronously by the format-specific transform (csv/geojson/geopackage/kml impls - outside this batch); HTTP response returns immediately with status `Running`.
    8. On completion: status `Completed`, `size` (bytes from fs.stat, undefined on stat error), `summary.observations/locations` ({count,startTimestamp,endTimestamp}). Info log `<username> exported data` {format, event name, counts}.
    9. On failure: delete file, status `Failed`, `archive.abort()`.
    
    List/read/delete: permission checks only require a principal present (`ensureGetMyExport*`); ownership enforced by querying `{_id, userId}`.
    
    ##### Data
    **Collection `exports`** (model `Export`, `adapters.exports.db.mongoose.ts`), versionKey off, `timestamps: { updatedAt: 'lastUpdated' }` (createdAt also kept):
    | field | type |
    |---|---|
    | _id | ObjectId |
    | userId | ObjectId ref User |
    | relativePath | String |
    | filename | String (never set by CreateExport) |
    | size | Number |
    | exportType | String required (format) |
    | status | 'Running'/'Completed'/'Failed' required |
    | options.eventId | Number ref Event required |
    | options.filter | Mixed (validated filter as above, Dates as BSON dates) |
    | processingErrors | [{type?:String, message:String, createdAt, updatedAt}] (no _id) - never written in this batch |
    | expirationDate | Date required |
    | summary.observations / summary.locations | {count:Number, startTimestamp:Date, endTimestamp:Date} |
    
    Repository reads/writes: `find().sort({_id:-1})` (getExports), `findOne({_id,userId}).populate(...)`, `find({userId}).sort({_id:'descending'}).populate(...)`, `create`, `findByIdAndUpdate(new:true)`, `findOneAndUpdate({_id,userId})`, `findByIdAndDelete`, `findOneAndDelete({_id,userId})`. Populate: `userId` select `_id username displayName`; `options.eventId` select `_id name`.
    
    **Expanded export entity** returned to clients: document fields plus `id`, `userId` (hex string), `user: {id, username, displayName}|null`, `options: {eventId:number, filter, event:{id,name}|null}`, plus `url`.
    
    **Filesystem**: `environment.exportDirectory` = `MAGE_EXPORT_DIR` || `/var/lib/mage/export`; file name `<id>-<exportType>.zip` (written by POST, read by GET, unlinked by DELETE).
    
    ##### Outputs & side effects
    - POST 200: export JSON (status Running) + `url: <req.getRoot()>/api/exports/mine/<id>`.
    - GET list 200: array of expanded exports each with `url`.
    - GET content 200 with headers `content-type: application/zip`, `content-length` only when `size` truthy; body streamed from file. 500 `{message:'unknown application response'}` if app returns neither error nor success.
    - DELETE 204 no body.
    - Errors: POST router uses `mageAppErrorHandler` (bare JSON string body); `/mine` router uses `compatibilityMageAppErrorHandler` (`{message}` body). Status map 403/404/400/500.
    - Writes zip file; updates Mongo status; info/error logs.
    
    ##### External calls
    - `archiver('zip')` library; format exporters from `ExportFactory` (app.impl.exports.csv/geojson/geopackage/kml — not traced here).
    - `resolveUserIsAnyOf(teamRepository, users, teams)` (app.impl.teams) to expand teams to user ids.
    - `EventPermissionServiceImpl.userHasEventPermission`.
    - Observation iteration via `IterateObservations` (search repo `findIdsByFilter` when `fieldFilter` present, then per-event observation repo `iterate`).
    
    ##### Migration notes
    - Export generation is fire-and-forget inside the request process; a server restart leaves Running records (handled by ExportArchiveTask startup sweep -> Failed).
    - Invalid-format after record creation is effectively unreachable because format is pre-validated against `EXPORT_FORMATS`, but if a factory lacks a format a Running orphan record is left.
    - Two different error body shapes on the same capability (string vs `{message}`).
    - `includeAttachments` defaults to true; `hasAttachments: false` collapses to undefined (no filter).
    - `favorites` filters to requester's favorites regardless of `users` list.
    - `deleteContent` errors are returned (not thrown) and ignored in DELETE — record removed even if file missing.
    - `content-length` header omitted when size is 0/undefined.
    - `url` uses `req.getRoot()` (scheme+host from request, defined on Express Request augmentation).
    - Download ownership: only the creating user can list/download/delete; there is no admin path here.

      export function ExportRoutes(appLayer: ExportAppLayer, createAppRequest: WebAppRequestFactory<EventRequest<UserWithRole>>): express.Router {
      
        const routes = express.Router()
      
        routes.route('/')
          .post(async (req, res, next) => {
            const params = parseExportCreateParams(req.body)
            if (params instanceof MageError) {
              return next(params)
            }
      
            const appReq: CreateExportRequest<UserWithRole> = createAppRequest<Omit<CreateExportRequest, 'context'>>(req, params)
            const appRes = await appLayer.createExport(appReq)
            if (appRes.success) {
              const response = jsonForExport(appRes.success, qualifiedBaseUrl(req))
              return res.json(response)
            }
            next(appRes.error)
          })
      
        routes.use(mageAppErrorHandler)
      
        return routes
      }
      
      function qualifiedBaseUrl(req: express.Request): string {
        return req.getRoot()
      }
      
      export function jsonForExport(e: Export, baseUrl: string): Export & { url: string } {
        return { ...e, url: `${baseUrl}/api/exports/mine/${e.id}`}
      }

    Commentary: CreateExport async pipeline and status transitions
    Code:
      export function CreateExport(
        exportFactory: ExportFactory,
        exportsRepository: ExportsRepository,
        contentStore: ExportStore,
        permissionService: api.ExportAppLayerPermissionService,
        teamRepository: TeamRepository,
        log: Logger = NoopLogger
      ): api.CreateExport {
        return async function createExport(req: api.CreateExportRequest): ReturnType<api.CreateExport> {
          return await withPermission<Export, KnownErrorsOf<api.CreateExport>>(
            permissionService.ensureCreateExportPermission(req.context),
            async (): Promise<Export | InvalidInputError> => {
              const user = req.context.requestingPrincipal()
              const { context, format, filter } = req
              const newExport = await exportsRepository.createExport({
                userId: user.id,
                eventId: context.mageEvent.id,
                ...req
              })
      
              const exporter = exportFactory(format)
      
              if (!exporter) {
                return invalidInput('invalid export type', [ `invalid export type: ${format}`, 'type' ])
              }
      
              const { content, relativePath } = contentStore.writeContent(newExport)
      
              const patch = {
                status: ExportStatus.Running,
                relativePath: relativePath
              }
              await exportsRepository.updateExportForUser(newExport.id, user.id, patch)
      
              const exportParams: ExportParams = {}
              if (filter?.observations) {
                const observations = filter.observations
                const observationUserIsAnyOf = await resolveUserIsAnyOf(teamRepository, observations.userIsAnyOf, observations.teamIsAnyOf)
                exportParams.observationParams = {
                  findSpec: {
                    where: {
                      stateIsAnyOf: [ 'active' ],
                      timestampAfter: observations.startDate,
                      timestampBefore: observations.endDate,
                      isFavoriteOfUser: observations.favorites ? user.id : undefined,
                      isFlaggedImportant: observations.important,
                      userIsAnyOf: observationUserIsAnyOf,
                      hasAttachments: observations.hasAttachments,
                      fieldFilter: observations.fieldFilter
                    },
                    includeAttachments: observations.includeAttachments
                  },
                  projection: observations.projection
                }
              }
      
              if (filter?.locations) {
                const locations = filter.locations
                const locationUserIsAnyOf = await resolveUserIsAnyOf(teamRepository, locations.userIsAnyOf, locations.teamIsAnyOf)
                exportParams.locationParams = {
                  findSpec: {
                    where: {
                      eventId: context.mageEvent.id,
                      timestampAfter: locations.startDate,
                      timestampBefore: locations.endDate,
                      userIsAnyOf: locationUserIsAnyOf
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
      
              const archive = archiver('zip')
              archive.pipe(content)
              exporter.export(context.mageEvent, archive, exportParams).then(async result => {
                const streamClosed = once(content, 'close')
                await archive.finalize()
                await streamClosed
                const stats = await contentStore.contentStats(newExport)
                const update = {
                  status: ExportStatus.Completed,
                  size: stats instanceof Stats ? stats.size : undefined,
                  summary: {
                    observations: { ...result.observations},
                    locations: { ...result.locations }
                  }
                }
                await exportsRepository.updateExportForUser(newExport.id, user.id, update)
                log.info(`${(user as { username?: string }).username ?? user.id} exported data`, {
                  format,
                  event: context.mageEvent.name,
                  observations: result.observations?.count ?? 0,
                  locations: result.locations?.count ?? 0
                })
              }).catch(async (err) => {
                log.error('Export error', err)
                await contentStore.deleteContent(newExport)
                await exportsRepository.updateExportForUser(newExport.id, user.id, { status: ExportStatus.Failed })
                archive.abort()
              })
      
              return { ...newExport, ...patch }
            }
          )
        }
      }

          },

          }

      }, exportSchemaOptions)
      
      export type ExportModelInstance = HydratedDocument<ExportDocument, object, object, object, typeof exportSchemaOptions>
      export type ExportModel = Model<ExportDocument, object, object, object, ExportModelInstance, typeof exportSchemaOptions>

    `modulesPathsInDir(dir)` in `service/src/utilities/loader.ts:10` is a shared bootstrap utility. It is invoked from three bootstrap sites, each at process start:
    1. `service/src/routes/index.js:11` — route factory exported as `module.exports = function(app, security)`, called from `service/src/express.ts:71-72` as `initializeRoutes(app, { authentication: auth })` (after `/private` static mount, before the global error handler).
    2. `service/src/models/index.js:111` — `initializeModels()`, called from `service/src/app.ts:557` before `migrate.runDatabaseMigrations(uri, options)`.
    3. `service/src/provision/index.js:57` — module-load-time side effect when `provision` is first `require`d.
    
    ##### Inputs
    - `dir: string` — absolute directory (always `__dirname` of the caller).
    - Directory listing via `fs.readdirSync(dir)` (fs-extra), names only (no recursion, no stat).
    - Filter keeps a filename only if ALL hold: does not start with `.`; matches `/\.(ts|js|json)$/`; does not match `/^index\./`; does not contain `.d.ts`; does not end in `.map`.
    - Returns names relative to `dir`, in `readdirSync` order (OS/filesystem order; alphabetical on ext4/APFS in practice, not guaranteed by Node).
    
    ##### Processing flow
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
      A[express.ts initializeRoutes app, auth] --> B[routes/index.js]
      B --> C[modulesPathsInDir __dirname]
      C --> D{for each file}
      D --> E[moduleName = file.slice 0, indexOf '.']
      E --> F[require './'+moduleName]
      F --> G{typeof initRoutes === 'function'?}
      G -- no --> H[throw Error 'does not provide a routes factory function']
      G -- yes --> I[initRoutes app, security]
      I --> D
      D -- done --> J[register app.param handlers: eventId,userId,teamId,iconId,deviceId,layerId,observationId]
      K[app.ts initializeModels] --> L[models/index.js] --> C2[modulesPathsInDir] --> M[require './'+moduleName - registers mongoose model]
      N[require provision] --> O[provision/index.js] --> C3[modulesPathsInDir] --> P[initStrategy provision -> provision.use strategy]
    ```
    **Route loading (routes/index.js):** files currently present: `authenticationconfigurations.js, devices.js, events.ts, imports.ts, layers.js, logins.js, observations.js, plugins.js, settings.js, setup.js, teams.js, users.js` (`index.js` and `routes.types.d.ts` are excluded). Each module must export `function(app, security)` that registers its own absolute URL paths (e.g. `devices.js` registers `/api/devices`, `/api/devices/count`, `/api/devices/:id` with `security.authentication.bearerAuthentication` + `access.authorize('READ_DEVICE')`). There is no URL prefix applied by the loader — each module owns its full path and its own auth middleware. `security` is `{ authentication: auth }`.
    
    After all route factories run, `routes/index.js` registers `app.param` resolvers:
    - `eventId`: must match `/^[0-9]+$/` else 400 `Invalid event ID in request path`; `Event.getById(eventId,{populate:false})`; missing → 404 `Event not found`; sets `req.event`. (DB error is ignored — treated as not found.)
    - `userId`: must match `/^[0-9a-f]{24}$/` else 400 `Invalid user ID in request path`; `new api.User().getById`; missing → 404 `User not found`; sets `req.userParam`.
    - `teamId`: no format check; `populate = req.query.populate == null || === 'true'`; `Team.getTeamById(teamId,{populate})`; missing → 404 `Team not found`; sets `req.team`.
    - `iconId`: `Icon.getById`; missing → 404 `Icon not found`; sets `req.icon`.
    - `deviceId`: `Device.getDeviceById`; missing → 404 `Device not found`; sets `req.device`.
    - `layerId`: `new api.Layer().getLayer(layerId)` promise; null → 404 `Layer not found`; rejection → `next(err)`; sets `req.layer`.
    - `observationId`: sets `req.observationId`; `new api.Observation(req.event).getById`; err → `next(err)`; missing → 404 `Observation not found`; sets `req.observation`. Depends on `req.event` already resolved (eventId param earlier in path).
    
    **Model loading (models/index.js):** logs `intializing database models ...`, then for each file (e.g. `authentication.js, authenticationconfiguration.js, counter.js, device.js, event.js, feature.js, icon.js, layer.js, login.js, observation.js, role.js, setting.js, team.js, token.js, user.js`; `.d.ts` excluded) `require('./'+moduleName)` purely for its side effect of `mongoose.model(...)` registration.
    
    **Provision loading (provision/index.js):** files `none.js`, `uid.js` (`index.d.ts`, `index.js`, and the `strategies` subdirectory excluded — directory has no matching extension). Each exports `function(provision)` which calls `provision.use(strategy)` (keyed by strategy name). No function-type check here — a non-function export throws TypeError on call.
    
    ##### Data
    No data store read/written by the loader itself. Reads directory listings only. Downstream: Mongoose model registrations (global mongoose singleton) and Express route table.
    
    ##### Outputs & side effects
    - Returns `string[]` of file names.
    - Callers: Express routes registered on `app`; `app.param` handlers; Mongoose models registered; provisioning strategies stored in `provision.strategies`. Logs `loading <name> routes from <file>` (debug), `intializing database model <name> ...` (info), `loading <name> provision strategy from <file>` (debug).
    - Throws synchronously (aborts startup) if a route module export is not a function.
    
    ##### External calls
    `fs.readdirSync` (fs-extra). Node `require` (dynamic). Downstream `Event.getById`, `api.User#getById`, `Team.getTeamById`, `Icon.getById`, `Device.getDeviceById`, `api.Layer#getLayer`, `api.Observation#getById` for param resolution.
    
    ##### Migration notes
    - **Capability-to-URL map is implicit**: the loader applies no prefix; to enumerate URLs you must read every route module. Redirecting `/api/exports` or any capability requires editing individual modules or inserting middleware before `initializeRoutes` in `express.ts`.
    - **Order dependence**: route registration order = `readdirSync` order, which determines Express matching precedence between modules for overlapping paths. Not guaranteed portable; pin explicitly in a re-implementation.
    - `moduleName` = text before the FIRST `.` — a file like `foo.bar.js` would be required as `./foo`. `.json` files pass the filter (would be required as JSON; for routes this then throws as non-function).
    - Works in both `src` (ts-node, `.ts` files) and compiled `lib` (`tsc -b src` emits `.js`; `build:copy_types` copies `.d.ts` into lib, which are excluded). `.js.map` excluded via `/\.map$/`.

    - `app.param` handlers are registered after routes; in Express 4 they still apply to all routes using those param names (looked up at dispatch).

    - Models must be loaded before migrations (`app.ts:557`) — migration code relies on registered models.
  Recommendation: Fully documented. For migration, replace dynamic discovery with an explicit, ordered route/model/strategy registry and confirm with the customer whether any deployment depends on drop-in route/strategy files being auto-discovered.

      export function modulesPathsInDir(dir: string): string[] {
        return fs.readdirSync(dir).filter(file => {
          return !(
            file[0] === '.' ||
            !/\.(ts|js|json)$/.test(file) ||
            /^index\./.test(file) ||
            /\.d\.ts/.test(file) ||
            /\.map$/.test(file)
          )
        });
      }

Only runtime importer: `service/src/models/device.js:9`, reached from `GET /api/devices` (`routes/devices.js`, middleware `bearerAuthentication` + `access.authorize('READ_DEVICE')`, handler `DeviceResource.prototype.getDevices`). `models/event.d.ts:5` imports the `PageInfo` type only (the actual `getMembers`/`getNonMembers` return a different `{pageSize,pageIndex,items,totalCount}` shape, not PageInfo).
    
    ##### Inputs
    - `countQuery`: Mongoose query (`Device.find(conditions)`).
    - `query`: Mongoose query to page (`Device.find(conditions)` with populate).
    - `options`: `{ limit, start, sort }` — `limit`/`start` numbers (route parseInt'd), `sort` a raw JSON **string** from `req.query.sort` (e.g. `{"name":1}`).
    - `dataKey`: property name for results (`'devices'`).
    - `dataConverter`: optional fn (always `null` from callers).
    - `count` (for `page`): precomputed total.
    
    Route-level inputs (`routes/devices.js getDevices`): query params `limit,start,sort,expand,page,page_size,term,state,includePagination,populate` plus any remaining keys used as filter. If `page` or `page_size` present: `limit = parseInt(page_size ?? '25')` (NaN→25), `start = (parseInt(page ?? '0') or 0 if NaN) * limit`; else `limit`/`start` parsed from `limit`/`start`. `state=registered|unregistered` → `filter.registered='true'|'false'`.
    
    ##### Processing flow
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
      R[GET /api/devices getDevices] --> G[Device.getDevices filter,expand,limit,start,sort]
      G --> P{options.limit != null && > 0}
      P -- no --> X[query.exec -> array]
      P -- yes --> U{expand.user && filter.user}
      U -- no --> CP[countAndPage Device.find conditions, query, options, 'devices']
      CP --> CD[countQuery.countDocuments] --> PG[page count, query, options, 'devices', null]
      U -- yes --> QU[queryUsersAndDevicesThenPage]
      QU --> UC[User.Model.countDocuments conditions] --> UF[User.Model.find conditions,'_id'] --> DQ[Device.find userId in ids, registered] --> DS[delete options.sort] --> PG
      PG --> S{options.sort?}
      S -- yes --> J[JSON.parse sort -> sort object]
      S -- no --> E[sort = {}]
      J --> L[limit=abs limit or 10; start=abs start or 0; page=ceil start/limit]
      E --> L
      L --> Q[query.sort.limit limit.skip limit*page.exec]
      Q --> C{dataConverter?} --> PI[build PageInfo]
      PI --> N{start+limit < count} -- yes --> NX[links.next = start+limit]
      PI --> PV{start > 0} -- yes --> PR[links.prev = abs options.start - options.limit]
    ```
    `page()` steps:
    1. `sort = {}`; if `options.sort` truthy, `JSON.parse(options.sort)` and copy each key/value (throws on invalid JSON → promise not created; synchronous throw propagates to route catch → `next(err)` → 500).
    2. `limit = Math.abs(options.limit) || 10`; `start = Math.abs(options.start) || 0`; `page = Math.ceil(start / limit)`.
    3. `query.sort(sort).limit(limit).skip(limit*page).exec()`.
    4. Apply `dataConverter` if given (never in practice).
    5. Build `PageInfo`: `{ links:{base:'',context:'',next:null,prev:null,self:''}, limit, size: data.length, start, [dataKey]: data, totalCount: count }`.
    6. `links.next = start+limit` if `< count`; `links.prev = Math.abs(options.start - options.limit)` if `start > 0`.
    
    `countAndPage()` = `countQuery.countDocuments()` then `page(count, query, options, dataKey, null)`.
    
    Route post-processing: if `includePagination` absent or `'false'` → `res.json(result.items || result)` (i.e. the whole PageInfo object when paged, or array when unpaged). Otherwise → `{ pageSize, page, totalCount, items }` where `items = result.items || result` and `totalCount = result.totalCount ?? result.count ?? items.length`.
    
    ##### Data
    - Reads `devices` collection (Mongoose `Device`): count with `conditions` from `FilterParser.parse(filter)` (+ `registered` boolean); find with same conditions, populated `userId` (full user if `expand=user`, else `displayName` only).
    - User-filter variant reads `users` collection: `countDocuments(conditions)` and `find(conditions, '_id')` populated `authenticationId.authenticationConfigurationId`; then devices with `{ userId: {$in: ids}, registered? }`, populated `userId`.
    - No writes. No cursor/stream; full `exec()` of one page.
    
    ##### Outputs & side effects
    Returns Promise<PageInfo>. No side effects except mutating `options` (`delete options.sort` in the user variant). `links.base/self` stay `''` here (only `transformers/pageinfo.js` fills them, which the devices route does not call).
    
    ##### External calls
    Mongoose `countDocuments`, `find`, `sort`, `limit`, `skip`, `populate`, `exec` on MongoDB.
    
    ##### Migration notes
    - **Skip rounds up**: `skip = limit * ceil(start/limit)`; `start` not a multiple of `limit` jumps to the next page boundary (start=5, limit=10 → skip 10), while `PageInfo.start` reports 5.
    - `limit` default 10 only inside `page()`; unpaged when route limit is undefined/0/negative (`isPaging` requires `> 0`), so `Math.abs` negative handling is effectively dead for devices.
    - `links.prev` uses raw `options.start - options.limit` (not defaulted values); can be > 0 but not clamped to 0 boundary semantics beyond `abs` (start=5, limit=10 → prev 5).
    - `sort` must be a JSON string; an object or malformed string throws. In the user-filter variant sort is silently dropped and **totalCount is the count of matching users, not devices**.
    - Route quirk: with `includePagination=true` and paging, `items` is the entire PageInfo object (it has no `.items`; devices are under `.devices`). Without `includePagination`, clients receive the raw PageInfo `{links,limit,size,start,devices,totalCount}`.
    - With `page`/`page_size` params, `page` param is zero-based.
    - `event.d.ts` claims `getMembers` returns `PageInfo`, but implementation returns `{pageSize,pageIndex,items,totalCount?}` — type declaration is inaccurate.
  Recommendation: Fully documented. Confirm with the customer whether clients depend on the round-up skip behaviour, the user-count totalCount in the expand=user&user=... variant, and the PageInfo-as-items response shape before normalizing pagination.

      DeviceResource.prototype.getDevices = async function (req, res, next) {
        try {
          const {
            populate,
            expand,
            limit,
            start,
            sort,
            includePagination,
            page,
            page_size,
            term,
            state,
            ...rawFilter
          } = req.query;
      
          const expandFlags = { user: /\buser\b/i.test(expand || '') };
      
          const filter = {
            ...rawFilter,
            ...(term ? { term } : {}),
            ...(state === 'registered'
              ? { registered: 'true' }
              : state === 'unregistered'
              ? { registered: 'false' }
              : {})
          };
      
          let effectiveLimit;
          let effectiveStart;
      
          const hasPageParams = page !== undefined || page_size !== undefined;
      
          if (hasPageParams) {
            const pageNum = parseInt(page ?? '0', 10);
            const pageSizeNum = parseInt(page_size ?? '25', 10);
      
            effectiveLimit = Number.isNaN(pageSizeNum) ? 25 : pageSizeNum;
            effectiveStart = (Number.isNaN(pageNum) ? 0 : pageNum) * effectiveLimit;
          } else {
            effectiveLimit = limit !== undefined ? parseInt(limit, 10) : undefined;
            effectiveStart = start !== undefined ? parseInt(start, 10) : undefined;
          }
      
          const result = await Device.getDevices({
            filter,
            expand: expandFlags,
            limit: effectiveLimit,
            start: effectiveStart,
            sort
          });
      
          const shouldIncludePagination =
            includePagination &&
            String(includePagination).toLowerCase() !== 'false';
      
          if (!shouldIncludePagination) {
            return res.json(result.items || result);
          }
      
          const items = result.items || result;
          const totalCount =
            result.totalCount ??
            result.count ??
            (Array.isArray(items) ? items.length : 0);
      
          let responsePageSize;
          let responsePage;
      
          if (hasPageParams) {
            responsePageSize = effectiveLimit || 25;
            responsePage = Math.floor((effectiveStart || 0) / responsePageSize);
          } else {
            responsePageSize =
              result.pageSize ||
              effectiveLimit ||
              result.limit ||
              25;
      
            responsePage =
              result.pageIndex ||
              result.page ||
              Math.floor((effectiveStart || 0) / responsePageSize);
          }
      
          const pagePayload = {
            pageSize: responsePageSize,
            page: responsePage,
            totalCount,
            items
          };
      
          return res.json(pagePayload);
